text:
NestTech - Ops: hi team, since the cert rotation yesterday we're seeing a lot of 502s from the hosted inference endpoint (api.redwood.example.com). Customer report: ~10% of requests return 502/gateway errors, curl shows SSL handshake timeouts. Happening across multiple regions. They say errors started ~2026-03-14T03:15Z after your cert rollout. Can we triage?

Priya S: thanks — can you paste a few failing request traces + curl output? rough time windows help.

NestTech - Ops: here's a sample from one failing run (macbook + curl from their infra):
```
$ curl -v https://api.redwood.example.com/v1/generate -H "Authorization: Bearer <redacted>" -d '{"prompt":"hi"}'
* Rebuilt URL to: https://api.redwood.example.com/v1/generate
*   Trying 18.205.22.14...
* TCP_NODELAY set
* Connected to api.redwood.example.com (18.205.22.14) port 443 (#0)
* ALPN, offering http/1.1
* Cipher selection: TLS_AES_128_GCM_SHA256
* SSL connection using TLSv1.3 / TLS_AES_128_GCM_SHA256
* TLS handshake timeout
* Failed to receive handshake
* Closing connection 0
curl: (35) SSL connect error
```

Priya S: ok that's consistent with handshake timeouts. did they capture `openssl s_client` output (we want SNI/servername, cert chain)?

NestTech - Ops: yes, they ran openssl around 03:18Z: 
```
$ openssl s_client -connect api.redwood.example.com:443 -servername api.redwood.example.com -showcerts
CONNECTED(00000003)
depth=0 CN=old-cert.redwood.example.com
verify error:num=20:unable to get local issuer certificate
---
no peer certificate
---
SSL handshake has read 0 bytes and written 321 bytes
---
```

Sam B: that `CN=old-cert.redwood.example.com` is interesting — suggests some clients/resolvers are hitting a backend still serving the old cert (maybe cached IP mapping to a host with a different cert). Do we have rollout logs for the cert rotation? Tomas, was there an A record/CNAME change?

Tomas R: we rotated the cert at 03:12Z and concurrently touched the edge autoscaling (small infra tweak). No DNS name changes planned — we only updated certs on the edge pool. TTLs are normally 300s.

Sam B: can you check DNS responses from the customer's resolver? I want to see if any resolver is returning an old IP that points to a host with the legacy cert.

NestTech - Ops: digging — they ran `dig +short api.redwood.example.com @their-resolver` during the spike and saw a mix of IPs: `18.205.22.14` and `34.203.10.9`. They say the old IP (34.203.10.9) returned the old cert when probed.

Priya S: ok two hypotheses: 1) resolver returned a stale DNS answer (caching longer than TTL) and that backend still had the old cert; 2) SNI mismatch / host header mapping causing the edge to select wrong cert for that connection. Both can produce handshake failures.

Eve L: oncall also seeing an increase in 502s from our metrics around 03:14-03:30Z. Spike correlates with cert rollout. I pulled the edge logs for 03:10-03:25Z and see a cluster of `tls: handshake timeout` traces plus a handful of `received connection with no cert` entries.

NetOps Bot: auto-detected: multiple upstreams serving mismatched certificate chains for hostname api.redwood.example.com between 03:12:00Z and 03:28:00Z. Affected IPs: [34.203.10.9, 18.205.22.14]. Suggest verifying host-level cert sync and resolver TTLs.

Sam B: please run from our vantage: `dig +noall +answer api.redwood.example.com @8.8.8.8` and `openssl s_client -connect <ip>:443 -servername api.redwood.example.com` for each returned IP. Also check whether our internal cert sync job skipped some nodes.

Tomas R: ran checks: our cert-sync job reported success across all edge nodes at 03:13Z, but there was a transient failure on the autoscaled pool that rejoined at 03:16Z — looks like one node booted with an older AMI image (outdated cert). That node was removed by autoscaler at 03:20Z. TTL of the DNS record is 300s but the customer's recursive resolver had a long cache (their support team confirmed a resolver cache override configured to 900s). So they held an old IP until ~03:27Z.

Priya S: that explains why some clients saw the old cert until ~03:27Z and got handshake timeouts. Workaround for customer: flush resolver cache or use alternate resolver (e.g., 8.8.8.8) until DNS caches expire. For immediate mitigation we routed traffic away from the problematic edge pool and applied a forced node drain to ensure no legacy AMIs are serving.

NestTech - Ops: can you confirm if any requests were billed but ended up failing? They reported some billing anomalies (charged for attempts even when 502 returned).

Priya S: 502s are gateway-level failures; depending on how their client retried, they might be billed for compute units only for successful token generation. I'll ask billing team to audit the logs for requests with final 5xx — we don't charge for incomplete token generation. Can you collect a few request ids (X-Request-ID) from their logs?

NestTech - Ops: provided request ids: r-6f2e, r-6f33, r-6f3a (all ~03:18Z).

Priya S: thanks. I've filed a billing review with those IDs — billing will follow up separately. From infra side: Tomas, status on forced drain and AMI rollout?

Tomas R: forced drain completed 03:30Z. I kicked off an immediate redeploy with the validated AMI across the pool. Post-redeploy health checks green at 03:35Z. We also updated the deployment runbook to block cert-change+autoscaler events in the same minute (lessons learned).

Sam B: action items: 1) add a preflight that verifies edge node image is the expected AMI before rotation; 2) add cross-check that cert thumbprint matches expected on all endpoints; 3) update customers/KB about long-resolver caches and recommend TTL best practices.

Eve L: can we add automated alerting for mixed cert chains across a hostname? NetOps Bot flagged it but we need an SLO alert: >0.5% mismatched cert responses in 5m -> page.

NetOps Bot: created alert ticket NET-872. Rule: periodic cert probing of all announced IPs + SNI check.

Priya S: final note to NestTech: we believe root cause was a combination of an autoscaled node rejoining with stale AMI (old cert) + the customer's recursive resolver caching an old IP longer than TTL. Mitigation applied and we deployed a fix. Apologies for the disruption — we will reach out via email with timeline and billing follow-up. :pray: 

NestTech - Ops: thanks for the fast triage. We'll flush our resolver cache and monitor. Please CC our security contact for the postmortem.

Tomas R: adding the PM/SE to the postmortem thread. Will attach config diffs and cert-sync logs.

Priya S: closing thread — marking as resolved in support system but will keep open for postmortem notes.

NetOps Bot: thread auto-tagged: "tls/dns;customer-impact;billing-review"
